claim: A classic zxnDMA job holds the bus and can hide the frame interrupt, which the simulator does not model; copy in short chunks or use the CPU when the copy would cover the interrupt line.
limit: Real-hardware timing is the real test.

evidence.text: 32-byte DMA copy lost an interrupt every few seconds in JNext (49.94 a second, one 40.5 ms gap); fixed by using DMA only when the copy ends 90 or more lines before the next interrupt.
Whole-view copy by zxnDMA in 8-row chunks, LDIR when the line is near the interrupt (the DMA hides the frame interrupt).
